rules.when: The task is a trivial mechanical edit: a rote rename, a formatting or lint sweep, a targeted typo or wording fix, a dependency version bump, or gathering files with no design judgement involved.
rules.why: Narrow, unambiguous work with an explicit bounded path. The cheapest fast profile is enough and this is the largest share of routine dispatches.

rules.when: The task is ordinary, well-scoped implementation work: a single feature or bug fix whose shape is already clear at intake, including carrying it through the full validation pipeline to a green PR.
rules.why: The default working profile. Most ship tasks land here, and the validation pipeline is the bulk of the token spend rather than the reasoning.

rules.when: The task is investigation, diagnosis, bug reproduction, planning, or an audit whose deliverable is knowledge rather than a code change.
rules.why: Ambiguous open-ended reasoning benefits from depth far more than from a larger model, and a scout produces no pipeline load to pay for.

rules.when: The task changes Firstmate's own shared tracked material: AGENTS.md, bin/, .agents/skills/, public skills/, CI workflows, or repo-level contracts.
rules.why: This surface carries safety boundaries and one-owner contracts, so a shallow profile is the wrong economy even when the diff looks small.

rules.when: The task is a large or ambiguous multi-file change, a risky refactor, a migration, work that must hold many interacting parts in mind at once, or work where an earlier attempt on a cheaper profile already failed.
rules.why: Genuinely hard work keeps the strongest reasoning class, but resolve the pair against current quota so a full session window falls back to depth on sonnet instead of burning extra usage.
